question.explanation:
First, we rewrite $27$ as $3^3$ to get:

\begin{align*} 3^{x} &= \dfrac{1}{27} \\[5pt] 3^{x} &= \dfrac{1}{3^3} \\[5pt] 3^{x} &= 3^{-3} \end{align*}

Now, since both sides of the equation share the same base $(3)$, we equate the exponents:

\begin{align*} 3^{\color{blue}x} &= 3^{\color{blue}-3} \\[5pt] {\color{blue}{x}} & = {\color{blue}-3} \end{align*}

Therefore, the solution is $x = -3.$

We need to isolate all terms with $m$ on one side of the equation. To do this, we subtract $4$ to both sides: \begin{align*} 2mn +m + 4&= 7 \\[5pt] 2mn +m + 4 - 4&= 7 - 4\\[5pt] 2mn + m &= 3 \end{align*}

Next, we factor out $m$ in the expression on the left-hand side. \begin{align*} 2mn + m&= 3 \\[5pt] m (2n+1)&= 3 \\[5pt] \end{align*}

Then, we divide both sides by $(2n+1)$ to isolate $m\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align*} \require{cancel} m (2n+1)&= 3 \\[5pt] \dfrac{m(2n+1)}{2n+1}&= \dfrac{3}{2n+1} \\[5pt] \dfrac{m\cancel{(2n+1)}}{\cancel{2n+1}} &=\dfrac{3}{2n+1} \\[5pt] m &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{3}{2n+1}} \end{align*}

Note: This result assumes that $2n+1\neq 0.$

question.text: Written in ascending order, the solutions to $|1-2x|-2=7$ are $x=$
question.explanation:
First, we isolate the absolute value on the left side of the equation: \begin{align*} |1-2x|-2&= 7 \\[5pt] |1-2x| &= 9 \end{align*}

Now, we have the following two cases:

  • If $|1-2x| = 1-2x,$ we obtain: \begin{align} |1-2x| &= 9 \\[5pt] 1-2x &= 9 \\[5pt] -2x &= 8 \\[5pt] x &= -4 \end{align}

  • If $|1-2x| = -(1-2x),$ we obtain: \begin{align} |1-2x| &= 9 \\[5pt] -(1-2x) &= 9 \\[5pt] -1 + 2x &= 9 \\[5pt] 2x &= 10 \\[5pt] x &= 5 \end{align}

Therefore, in ascending order, the solutions are $x=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-4}$ and $x=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{5}.$

question.text: Order the sides of the triangle $\triangle RST$ above from the shortest to the longest.
question.explanation:
First, let's find the missing angle $T.$ Since the interior angles of a triangle sum to $180^\circ,$ we have \begin{align*} m\angle{R}+m\angle{S}+m\angle{T} &= 180^\circ \\[3pt] 40^\circ + 103^\circ + m\angle T & = 180^\circ \\[3pt] m\angle T &= 180^\circ - 143^\circ\\[3pt] m\angle T &= 37^\circ. \end{align*}

Since $\angle T$ is the smallest angle, its opposite side $\overline{RS}$ is the shortest side of the triangle.

Since $\angle S$ is the largest angle, its opposite side $\overline{RT}$ must be the longest side of the triangle.

So, we have

\[ RS < ST < RT \] and therefore, the required order is \[\overline{RS}, \overline{ST}, \overline{RT}.\]

question.text: The solution to the inequality $-2a\ge 10$ is $a$
question.explanation:
The variable $a$ is being multiplied by $-2.$ To isolate $a,$ we perform the opposite operation, which is dividing by $-2.$ Remember to perform the same operation on both sides.

Also, when multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

\begin{align} -2a \,\,&{\color{blue}\ge}\,\, 10 \\[5pt] \dfrac{-2a}{-2} \,\,&{\color{red}\le}\,\, \dfrac{10}{-2} \\[5pt] \dfrac{-2a}{-2} \,\,&{\color{red}\le}\,\, {-5} \end{align}

Now, we can cancel a common factor of $-2$ from both the numerator and denominator.

\begin{align} \require{cancel} \dfrac{-2a}{-2} &\le {-5} \\[5pt] \dfrac{\cancel{-2}a}{\cancel{-2}} &\le {-5} \\[5pt] a &\le {-5} \end{align}

Therefore, the solution is $a\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\leq} \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-5}.$

question.text:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the angles shown above?

  1. $m\angle AOB = m\angle BOC$
  2. $m\angle BOC = m\angle COD$
  3. $\angle AOB \cong \angle DOE$
question.explanation:
From the diagram, we see that

  • $\angle AOB$ and $\angle BOC$ are marked with $|$, and

  • $\angle COD$ and $\angle DOE$ are marked with $||.$

Therefore, \begin{align*} \angle AOB &\cong \angle BOC \\[5pt] \angle COD &\cong \angle DOE. \end{align*}

Consequently, we have

\begin{align*} m\angle AOB &= m\angle BOC \\[5pt] m\angle COD &= m\angle DOE. \end{align*}

So statement I is true, while statements II and III are false.
